content.comment_body: Can the [product_name] show string values on its display? I've checked the forum but couldn't find anything on this topic. Hardware: [product_name] [article_no] Software: [version_no] In my project, I use an up/down counter to select different modes. The user presses a momentary push button to scroll through mode levels: - If count = 0, mode = off - If count = 1, mode = low - If count = 2, mode = medium - If count = 3, mode = high The logic itself is working, but I want to make the GUI easier for users. On the display, I can show the counter values 1, 2, 3. But is there any way to have the display show those numbers as string values like "low", "medium", "high"—without creating duplicate screens for each word? Thanks in advance! Cheers,

No, that's not possible with the current options. You can add I/O status names to message texts. You can show the status of a digital operand (either 0 or 1), and for each state display an 8-character text, but that's the current limit.
Here's a small example that may help. It uses four I/O state names for feedback.

Thanks [user_name]! I'm aware of that feature, but was hoping for something like a 'string block.' Maybe future versions will include this feature. For this project, I’ll create separate screens and have the mode change the word displayed. That keeps the mode in the same position on the display. Thank you for your reply and suggestion! Cheers,

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing restrictions with [product_name] display functionality when trying to show dynamic string feedback linked to numeric values (such as mapping counts to mode names). Currently, only I/O status names (with a two-state limit and short text) can be shown, which limits visual feedback and can require extra screens for more advanced UI needs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a feature allowing direct mapping and display of various string values to numeric counter outputs for easier, clearer GUI operation and fewer redundant screens.
